newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bids at 3-yr Portugal bond auction seen 5.85-6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bids at 3-yr Portugal bond auction seen 5.85-6 pct.

text.p: Bids at Tuesday's auction of three-year fixed rate Portuguese bonds are expected to be between 5.85 and 6.0 percent, but analysts were unsure whether the Public Credit Management Institute (IGCP) would accept the bids.
They said it was unlikely the IGCP would place all 25 billion escudos ($146.3 million) on offer. Auction results are due around 1100 GMT.
"The bidding will have to take into consideration what has happened in the secondary market and so, the bulk of the bids will be between 5.90 and 6.0 percent," said a fixed-rate director.

Another dealer said "There could be some bids as low as 5.85 percent, but they will be few. This raises doubts about whether the IGCP will accept the bids and whether the maximum accepted rate will be 5.95 or 6.00 percent."
At the last auction on February 12, the IGCP placed these bonds at an average weighted interest rate of 5.4972 percent. The maximum accepted rate was 5.50 percent and the minimum was 5.40 percent.
On Monday, February 2000 bonds, the benchmark bonds in the three-year series, closed to yield 5.97 percent, giving a positive yield spread of 16 basis points over March 2000 Bonos.
-- Sergio Goncalves, Lisbon newsroom, 351-1-3150035 ($ = 170.8 Portugese Escudos)
